podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Life and Family (1962-1991)
podcast.body: Dave Gahan's biological father, Jack, left the family when Dave was only six months old and died in 1991, just as Dave was attempting to reconnect with him. He was married to Joanne Fox, who helped establish the first official Depeche Mode fan club, and they had a son named Jack, but Dave rarely saw his son during the first five years of his life due to touring. "Dave also lost his biological father, Jack, who left the family when Dave was 6 months old."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Post-World Violation Tour Mental State (1990-1992)
podcast.body: Following the World Violation Tour, Dave Gahan became notably angry and irritable, compounded by undiagnosed ADD and autistic traits. He was forced to move twice due to relentless fan intrusion at his home. "Dave Gahn was especially angry and irritable."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Devotional Tour Behavior and Arrest (1993)
podcast.body: During the Devotional Tour, Dave Gahan's ego spiraled, prompting other band members to insist on separate hotel floors. He engaged in heavy heroin use, was rumored to have a "vampire phase" involving coffin naps, and was arrested on September 8, 1993, in Quebec City for fighting with security guards at a hotel. "Dave and the band's road manager were arrested after fighting with security guards at a hotel in Quebec City on September 8, 1993."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Overdose and Heart Attack in New Orleans (October 8, 1993)
podcast.body: In New Orleans, Dave Gahan overdosed between the main set and the encore, suffering a heart attack that required paramedics to rush him to the hospital, leading Martin Gore to perform a solo song for the encore. Dave recalled hearing the song "Death's Door" in the background during this near-fatal incident. "At the end of the gig, I couldn't go back for the encore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Physical Decline and Stage Injuries (1993-1994)
podcast.body: Despite training for the Devotional Tour with workouts, running, and martial arts, Dave Gahan looked terrible due to his drug use, with needle marks visible on his arms. Later in the tour, his stage performances became erratic, leading to forgotten lyrics and miscues, and he needed cortisone shots for his voice. He weighed no more than 100 pounds by the summer of 1994 and was hospitalized after a stage dive in Detroit. "So great was the abuse on his body that by the summer of 1994, Dave Gein weighed no more than 100 pounds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Post-Devotional Tour Relapse and Home Invasion (1994-1995)
podcast.body: After the tour, Dave returned to Los Angeles, continuing his heavy drug use. He eventually woke up on a dealer's lawn wearing only pants, shoes, and socks, having been robbed of his wallet, watch, jewelry, and shirt. Later, his house was completely looted while he was away at rehab, losing all his possessions, including recording gear and kitchen cutlery. "One morning he woke up on a dealer's lawn wearing nothing but pants, shoes and socks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: First Suicide Attempt (1995)
podcast.body: At the Sunset Marquis Hotel, Dave Gahan slashed his wrists with two-inch cuts while on the phone with his mother. An ambulance was called, and paramedics had to stitch him up on the spot without anesthetic due to the critical situation. This was not his first rescue by the same paramedic team, who began calling him "the cat" for his multiple near-death experiences. "While looking in the bathroom mirror, slashing his wrists seemed like a good idea."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Paranoia and Escalating Drug Use (1995-1996)
podcast.body: Dave Gahan's paranoia intensified, leading him to carry a gun, even to check his mailbox. He developed bizarre habits like watching the Weather Channel for 24 hours, painting his walls and floors black, and conversing with stuffed animals that he believed talked back. He also began injecting powerful speedballs (heroin and cocaine) to feel anything. "He grew paranoid and carried a gun with him even if it were just outside to check the mailbox."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Psychiatric Ward and Second Suicide Attempt (1995)
podcast.body: After his first suicide attempt, Dave Gahan woke up in a straightjacket in a padded room at the psychiatric ward of Cedar Sinai Hospital, his only thought being to get high again. He later attempted to hang himself in his bathroom, but that attempt also failed. "When he woke up in a straight jacket in a padded room in the psychiatric ward at nearby Cedar Sinai Hospital, all he could think about was getting high again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: 1996 Clinical Death Experience
podcast.body: On May 27, 1996, Dave Gahan overdosed on what appeared to be a speedball in a villa at the Sunset Marquis Hotel. Paramedics were called at 1:15 a.m. and had to revive him three times. He was clinically dead for two minutes, his heart having stopped. "Paramedics were able to revive him not once, not twice but three times and when he finally regained consciousness he asked the EMTs if he'd OD'd again and they replied no you were clinically dead for two minutes. His heart had stopped."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Clinical Death at Sunset Marquis (May 28, 1996)
podcast.body: Dave Gahan died for a couple of minutes on May 28, 1996, in one of the second-floor villas at the Sunset Marquis in Los Angeles. At the time, he was struggling with a "paranoid drug hell" and had injected a powerful "speedball" (a mix of red rum, heroin, and cocaine), leading to a massive overdose and cardiac arrest. Paramedics were called after a woman, whose identity is unknown, found him unresponsive, and he was clinically dead for a six-minute window before being revived, which ultimately scared him straight. "It was here at the Sunset Marquis that Dave Gahn died for a couple of minutes on May 28, 1996."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Near-Fatal Overdose and Clinical Death (May 27-28, 1996)
podcast.body: After flying back to Los Angeles from recording sessions for "Sister of Night," Dave Gahan injected a mixture of heroin and cocaine at the Sunset Marquis Hotel. He suffered a massive overdose, turning blue and his breathing slowing. At 1:15 AM on May 28, 1996, paramedics found him clinically dead for two minutes due to full cardiac arrest. He was revived by an adrenaline needle to the heart, similar to a scene from "Pulp Fiction." "Dave gone was dying."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Out-of-Body Experience (1996)
podcast.body: During his clinical death in 1996, Dave Gahan recounted an experience where he remembered only darkness, followed by a "humongous voice" stating, "this is wrong like I don't get to choose when this is over." He also described exiting his body, floating under the ceiling, and observing paramedics trying to save him, feeling like his soul was screaming and witnessing the events unfold for what seemed like hours. "In the hospital Dave says the first thing I remember was that I exited my body. I was floating underneath the ceiling and I could observe what was happening to me. People were running around my body trying to save me. I believe it was my soul screaming which had already left my body. It became a witness to what happened to me. These seconds seemed like hours to me and then suddenly there was complete frightening darkness around me."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Clinical Death Relapse and Recovery (1996)
podcast.body: Despite being released from the hospital and jail on $10,000 bail for drug charges after his near-fatal overdose, Dave Gahan immediately returned to using heroin, though it no longer provided any buzz. This realization prompted him to check into the Exodus Recovery Center in Marino Del Rey, California, a facility where Kurt Cobain and Shannon Hoon also sought treatment. In Dave's case, the treatment was successful, leading to his sobriety. "But in Dave's case, the treatment worked."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: "The Cat" by LA Paramedics
podcast.body: Due to his numerous overdoses and instances where he narrowly escaped death, LA Paramedics gave Dave Gahan the nickname "the cat," implying that he seemed to possess many lives. "LA Paramedics started calling him the cat because he seemed to have so many lives."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Divorce from Teresa Conroy (Late 1990s)
podcast.body: After Dave Gahan achieved sobriety, his second wife, Teresa Conroy, filed for divorce, seeking a significant financial settlement. This marked Dave's second divorce. "Meanwhile, Teresa filed for divorce and wanted some big money."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Early 90s Drug Abuse
podcast.body: In the early 1990s, Dave Gahan was described as "totally out of control," with a primary addiction to heroin, though he experimented with nearly all types of drugs. His substance abuse was so severe that it contributed to a chaotic environment during the 1993-94 Devotional Tour. "Back in the early 90s Dave was totally out of control. The heroin mostly but he tried almost anything."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Escalating Drug Use and Physical Decline (Early 1990s)
podcast.body: Dave Gahan's drug intake, primarily cocaine and heroin, escalated to intravenous use, causing him to stop eating and become dangerously thin. He grew out his hair and acquired numerous tattoos, often while so high he couldn't remember getting them, including one that read "T.C. TTM-FG" for Teresa Conroy. "His body had become so hardened to the drug that it had no effect, but he had to keep using just to keep from getting dope sick."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Heroin Addiction and Distinctive Tattoos (Early 1990s)
podcast.body: Dave Gahan and Teresa Conroy became recognizable heroin junkies, with one of their favorite wedding presents being a lump of black tar heroin. Dave's body bore multiple tattoos, including one on his shoulder blades that took a single 10-hour sitting, often acquired while he was heavily intoxicated. "There's one that reads T.C. TTM-FG, and stands for Teresa Conroy to the Mother Effor Dave God."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Initial Apprehension for Solo Endeavor
podcast.body: Gahan admitted that the idea of undertaking a solo project on his own "really kind of freaked him out." "The thought of doing it all really kind of freaked him out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Long Incubation Period for Solo Debut
podcast.body: It took Dave Gahan 22 years to release his first solo album while being a member of Depeche Mode. "It took him 22 years to get around to it. But at least he did it, right?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Motivation for Solo Work After Near-Death Experiences
podcast.body: After a period of "recovery and resurrection" following multiple "near-death experiences in the 1990s," Gahan felt compelled to "test myself in a positive way" by recording his own album with his own songs, despite initial trepidation. "But after Dave's recovery and resurrection following a series of near-death experiences in the 1990s, you see thought, you know, maybe it's time I tested myself in a positive way and recorded my own album with my own songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Move to Los Angeles and Drug Initiation (Early 1990s)
podcast.body: After a personal crisis and his first divorce from Joanne Fox, Dave Gahan moved to Los Angeles, where he fully embraced the "Rock God" fantasy. He began using heroin around 1991 and quickly escalated his drug use after meeting Teresa Conroy, who introduced him to the drug-heavy Jane's Addiction crowd. "Right around the time he first started using heroin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Multiple Overdoses and Suicide Attempt
podcast.body: Dave Gahan experienced several overdoses during the Devotional Tour, including one incident between the main set and the encore that rendered him unconscious. His drug use escalated after the tour, leading to paranoia, conversations with stuffed animals, carrying a gun, and a suicide attempt in August 1995 where he slashed his wrists. "Dave managed to overdose a couple of times on the tour including one occasion where a bump between the main set and the encour knocked him cold. There was a suicide attempt in August 1995 when he slashed his wrists and there were plenty of overdoses."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Near-Fatal Overdose and Court-Ordered Rehabilitation
podcast.body: During the recording process for Ultra, Dave Gahan experienced a severe overdose that nearly cost him his life, resulting in another hospitalization. This terrifying event, combined with court intervention, compelled him to enter a mandatory rehabilitation program. This forced rehabilitation was a crucial turning point, not only saving his life but also the future of Depeche Mode. "Se produzo una de las enormes sobre dosis que tiene que valo hospital en la que casi se muere y empieza un poco el resurgir del cantante."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Depeche Mode -  Ultra. Punto de inflexión de la banda

podcast.title: Physical Deterioration and Vocal Performance on Ultra
podcast.body: During the period of Ultra's creation and release, Dave Gahan was visibly deteriorated physically, as evidenced in the album's music videos where he appeared in a "truly lamentable state." His vocal performance on the album is described as the saddest, most exhausting, and most decadent of his entire career, reflecting his near-death experience and the profound emotional and physical toll of his addiction. "Vemos ahí un Dave Bajan tan deteriorado físicamente en los video clips pero ya incluso en su voz lo hemos tan apagado, tan rendido, tan alborde de la muerte."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Depeche Mode -  Ultra. Punto de inflexión de la banda

podcast.title: Reflections on Addiction and Sobriety (Ongoing)
podcast.body: Dave Gahan reflected on his period of addiction as a "negative way of a permanent solution to a temporary problem," akin to living a constant suicide. He acknowledged the fear of change and the comfort found in misery, and the struggle to regain a sense of normalcy and happiness without drugs. He credited working with a vocal coach for providing confidence, self-worth, and daily structure in his recovery. "Trying to destroy myself is a really negative way of a permanent solution to a temporary problem."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Rehab and Sobriety
podcast.body: Following his near-fatal overdose and subsequent arrest on drug charges in 1996, Dave Gahan faced a choice between a one-year rehab program or two years in jail. He chose rehab and has maintained his sobriety ever since. "Then Dave was arrested on drug charges. He ended up on a one-year rehab trip. It was either that or spend two years in jail. The good news was that Dave has been sober ever since."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Relationship and Marriage to Teresa Conroy (Early 1990s)
podcast.body: Dave Gahan became involved with Teresa Conroy, Depeche Mode's former press officer, who introduced him to the Jane's Addiction social circle where drugs were readily available. They were described as "rock and roll soulmates," indulging in the rockstar lifestyle and having a baby daughter together. They married at the Graceland Chapel in Las Vegas by an Elvis impersonator in April 1992. "He also hooked up with Teresa Conroy, the Pesh Mode's former press officer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Severe Heroin Addiction (Mid-1990s)
podcast.body: In the mid-1990s, Dave Gahan suffered from a life-threatening heroin addiction, which led to multiple hospitalizations due to overdoses. This addiction rendered him physically debilitated and made recording new music with Depeche Mode, particularly for the album Ultra, extremely challenging, almost leading to his expulsion from the band. His struggle was a major factor in the band's critical period and his appearance in the Ultra music videos reflected his poor physical state. "Él estaba en un tan nivel de adició a la heroína y un estado físico tan debleque que trabajar con él era prácticamente imposible."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Depeche Mode -  Ultra. Punto de inflexión de la banda

podcast.title: Supervised Recording of Ultra
podcast.body: Dave Gahan's rehabilitation process was so critical that judicial authorities supervised the recording sessions for Depeche Mode's album Ultra. This oversight was deemed necessary due to the significant presence of heroin, alcohol, and other drugs during the band's recording processes at that time, highlighting the severe environment they were in. The intervention ultimately helped save the band from dissolution and Gahan from potential death. "La sonidad de Santinar Códipo estuvieron supervisando la grabación de la Albuo Muttra porque había tal cantidad de heroína, de alcohol y de drogas en los procesos de grabación de Petchmode en esa época."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Depeche Mode -  Ultra. Punto de inflexión de la banda

podcast.title: Vampire Conspiracy Theory
podcast.body: The theory that Dave Gahan is a vampire arose in the early 90s due to his wasted appearance from heroin and cocaine addiction, his belief in his own "rock god hype," and his commissioning of a coffin-shaped bed for pre-show naps on tour. Further fueling the rumor was an alleged incident where he bit a journalist on the neck backstage, along with bizarre behaviors like painting his entire house black. Pictures of a "vampiric looking" Gahan with fangs circulated as the public internet was emerging. Gahan himself stated in a 2001 interview that he "definitely could have been a vampire in my own head," confirming he slept in a huge double coffin-shaped bed in Los Angeles, describing his life at the time as "Spinal Tap." "I definitely could have been a vampire in my own head. Even the bed I slept in in Los Angeles was in the shape of a coffin, a huge double bed shaped like a coffin. My whole life was spinal tap at that time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-World Violation Tour Hiatus and Fan Intrusion (1990-1992)
xref.body: After the demanding World Violation Tour, Depeche Mode took an 18-month break. During this period, Dave Gahan faced extreme fan intrusion, having to move twice because fans frequently appeared on his lawn, with one even hiring a private detective to find his home address. "Once that tour wrapped up, Depeche Mode took a little time off and they needed it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Heroin Addiction Begins (1991)
xref.body: Dave Gahan's heroin addiction began around 1991 after he moved to Los Angeles and became involved with the Jane's Addiction social circle, living a rock and roll lifestyle with his wife, Teresa. A wedding gift they received for their wedding was a lump of black tar heroin. "Heroin was Dave's thing, starting in about 1991."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Isolation During Devotional Tour (1993)
xref.body: During the North American leg of the Devotional Tour, Dave Gahan's increasingly insufferable ego and "rock god" persona led the other band members to insist on staying on separate floors in hotels to manage the extreme tension. "He became so unsufferable that when it came to staying in hotels, the other members of the group insisted on being on separate floors from Dave."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Banned from Berlin's Intercontinental Hotel (June 1993)
xref.body: During the Devotional Tour's stop in Berlin in June 1993, Depeche Mode was banned from the Intercontinental Hotel, their usual accommodation, due to Dave Gahan's behavior, which included spending days injecting heroin in his room. "In June 1993, when the tour rolled into Berlin, the Pesh Mode was banned from the intercontinental hotel, which was their usual place."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Dave Gahan and Darabomonte Arrested in Montreal (September 8, 1993)
xref.body: On September 8, 1993, Dave Gahan and touring keyboardist Darabomonte were arrested and jailed in Montreal after Dave punched a hotel concierge. This incident occurred after a loud party in their suite led to numerous complaints, prompting the hotel to cut their power. "September 8, 1993. Dave Cajon and Touring Keyboard as Darabomonte are arrested and jailed after Dave punched the concierge of a Montreal hotel in the mouth."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Mid-Show Heart Attack (October 8, 1993)
xref.body: On October 8, 1993, Dave Gahan suffered a heart attack mid-show in New Orleans but remarkably managed to finish the set before being removed backstage by paramedics. "Dave is removed from backstage at a show in New Orleans by paramedics after he suffered a heart attack. He actually had a heart attack mid-show, but he somehow managed to finish the set."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Devotional Tour Environment (1993-94)
xref.body: The Depeche Mode Devotional Tour in 1993-94 was marked by significant debauchery, particularly from Dave Gahan, which reportedly "scared straight" the opening act, Primal Scream. The tour environment was so intense that it featured both its own drug counselor and a drug dealer, alongside frequent run-ins with the police. "The tour had both its own drug counselor and drug dealer. There were run-ins with the cops."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Devotional Tour European Leg (May 19 – July 31, 1993)
xref.body: The Devotional Tour kicked off on May 19, 1993, in Lille, France, marking the beginning of an 11-week European leg that concluded on July 31 in London. Throughout this period, relations among the four band members remained highly strained, with significant concern focused on singer Dave Gahan. "Depeche Mode's devotional tour began on May 19, 1993 in Lil France, the start of an 11-week European tour that ended in London on July 31."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Devotional Tour Vampire Phase (1993)
xref.body: Dave Gahan reportedly entered a "vampire phase" during the Devotional Tour, keeping his dressing room dark and filled with candles. As a joke, a coffin was delivered to the tour, which Dave Gahan used to take naps before each show. "There was a rumor that Dave went through a vampire phase, his dressing room was dark and filled with candles, and as a joke, someone delivered a coffin to the tour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Drug-Induced Heart Attack and Paranoia (1993-1994)
xref.body: During the 1993 tour for "Songs of Faith and Devotion," Dave Gahan's heroin use became so severe he spent days injecting himself in hotel rooms, leading to a mild heart attack in New Orleans that prevented him from performing an encore. After the tour, he returned to LA, experiencing deep drug paranoia, carrying a gun everywhere, watching the Weather Channel for 24 hours straight, and hallucinating conversations with his stuffed animals. "Drugs had brought on a mild heart attack."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Opening Act for Depeche Mode (1993)
xref.body: Primal Scream opened for Depeche Mode on their 1993 "Songs of Faith and Devotion" tour, where they were reportedly frightened by the severity of Dave Gahan's heroin addiction, indicating Gahan's drug use was extreme even by their standards. "His appetite for drugs was so great on the songs of Faith and Devotion Tour in 1993 that he even scared the guys in the opening act primal scream."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Primal Scream's Shocking Experience (1993)
xref.body: Dave Gahan reportedly insisted that Primal Scream open for Depeche Mode on the Devotional Tour because he knew they enjoyed partying. However, Primal Scream was so appalled by the level of drug use and excess they witnessed that they allegedly gave up drugs entirely, despite their prior extensive use. "The story goes that primal scream was so shocked by what they saw that they gave up drugs entirely."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Shocked by Depeche Mode's Excess (1993)
xref.body: Primal Scream served as an opening act for Depeche Mode's Devotional Tour at Dave Gahan's insistence, as he believed they shared a similar partying spirit. However, the band was reportedly so shocked by the extreme drug use they witnessed that their singer, Bobby Gillespie, was quoted saying Dave Gahan did more drugs than all of Primal Scream combined, leading them to give up drugs entirely. "The story goes that primal scream was so shocked by what they saw that they gave up drugs entirely."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Stage Fall (July 1994)
xref.body: In July 1994, Dave Gahan fell 12 feet off the stage in Indianapolis, resulting in multiple broken ribs. "We might as well include the time in July of 1994 when he fell 12 feet off the stage in Indianapolis and broke a bunch of ribs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death and Rehab Attempt (1994)
xref.body: Kurt Cobain's death was reported on April 8, 1994, affecting Dave Gahan during Depeche Mode's tour in Buenos Aires. Cobain had also attempted to get clean at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marino Del Rey, California, a week before his death. "De Peshmoan was in Buenos Aires on April 8, 1994 when they heard about the death of Kurt Cobain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Kurt Cobain's Death Impact (April 8, 1994)
xref.body: While in Buenos Aires on April 8, 1994, Depeche Mode learned of Kurt Cobain's death. Dave Gahan was reportedly taken aback by the news for a day or two before reverting to his usual drug-fueled habits. "De Peshmoan was in Buenos Aires on April 8, 1994 when they heard about the death of Kurt Cobain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Near-Death Experience and Recovery (1995-1996)
xref.body: From late spring 1995 through to a brief clinical death in 1996, Dave Gahan's life was consumed by heroin addiction, costing $3,000 daily, leading to extreme dissociation, conversations with stuffed animals (including a Bugs Bunny doll), and two suicide attempts. On May 27, 1996, after an attempt to record with Martin Gore, Gahan injected cocaine and heroin at the Sunset Marquis Hotel in Hollywood, leading to full cardiac arrest and two minutes of clinical death. He recalled a vision of his wife screaming for him to return and a voice stating, "This is wrong, you don't get to decide." His recovery began after summer 1996, largely influenced by the threat of green card revocation from the American government if he didn't enter rehab and remain sober. He has been sober since June 6, 1996, now runs four times a week, lives in New York's West Village, and is married to Jennifer, his third wife. "He was for all intents and purposes clinically dead for two full minutes. He now says he remembers the vision of his wife screaming at him to come back to this plane."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: House Looting Post-Rehab (1995)
xref.body: After a period at a rehabilitation clinic in the Arizona desert, Dave Gahan was released on August 27, 1995. Upon returning to his house, he discovered it had been completely looted and burglarized. This incident immediately prompted him to use heroin ("smack") and check into the Sunset Marquis hotel. "But when he checked out on August 27, 1995 and returned to his house, he found that it had been completely looted, burgl'd."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Suicide Attempts and Overdose (1995-1996)
xref.body: While staying at the Sunset Marquis hotel in August 1995, Dave Gahan attempted suicide by slashing his wrists in the bathroom mirror. After waking in a psychiatric ward, his primary focus was getting high again, seemingly indifferent to the fact that a suicide attempt was a felony in California. He later made another unsuccessful attempt to hang himself in his bathroom. His struggles culminated on May 27, 1996, when after attending a party and checking back into the Sunset Marquis, he injected a mixture of heroin and cocaine, resulting in a massive overdose. At 1:15 AM on May 28, an unknown person called 911, and paramedics found him clinically dead for two minutes due to full cardiac arrest. "When he woke up in the psychiatric ward, all he could think about was getting high again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Overdose Recovery (1996)
xref.body: Following his release from the hospital and subsequently from jail on drug charges after his massive overdose in May 1996, Dave Gahan immediately returned to using heroin ("smack"). However, this time, he experienced no "buzz" or effect from the drug. This profound lack of sensation prompted him to voluntarily admit himself to the Exodus Recovery Center in Marina del Rey, California, a facility notably known for having treated Kurt Cobain shortly before his death. At Exodus, Gahan embraced accountability for his actions, achieved sobriety, cleaned up, and has reportedly maintained a clean and straight lifestyle since late 1998. "But this time, there was no buzz. There was nothing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Long-Term Recovery and Current Status (1997-Present)
xref.body: Depeche Mode eventually overcame the tumultuous period between 1991 and 1997. Dave Gahan and Martin Gore are now sober, and Alan Wilder is living a quiet life. While Andy Fletcher died in 2022, Martin Gore and Dave Gahan continue to record and tour together, showing intent to move forward almost 50 years after the band's formation. "The good news is that the Pesh mode eventually came out on the other side of all things that happened between 1991 and 1997."

xref.title: "Scared Straight" by Depeche Mode's Debauchery
xref.body: Primal Scream, who opened for Depeche Mode on much of their 1993-94 Devotional Tour, was reportedly "scared straight" by the intense drug use and debauchery displayed by Dave Gahan and the rest of Depeche Mode during that period. "Primo's scream who opened up much of the 93 94 devotional tour was scared straight by Dave and the rest of Dopech Mode's debutshery."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: "The Cat" Nickname
xref.body: Los Angeles paramedics nicknamed Dave Gahan "the cat" due to his four near-death experiences with drugs. "Even though he's come close four times, this is why Los Angeles paramedics call him the cat."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Andy Fletcher's Quiet Demeanor
xref.body: Andy Fletcher was known as the "quiet one" in Depeche Mode, content to let Dave Gahan and Martin Gore handle most of the speaking during interviews. "Andy was the quiet one in Depeche Mode."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Assisted Dave Gahan's Solo Debut
xref.body: Knox Chandler, a friend of Dave Gahan, provided help and coaching that enabled Gahan to slowly bring his first solo album, Paper Monsters, to fruition. "But thanks to a friend named Knox Chandler, who helped and coached him, a record slowly came together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Members' Current Residences
xref.body: Martin Gore resides in Santa Barbara, California, where his ex-wife owns a spa. Dave Gahan lives in New York, and Andrew Fletcher has his home in the Maidstone area of London. "So we got Martin living in California. There's Dave in New York and Andrew in London."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's "Gesh" Piercing
xref.body: Dave Gahan once sported a "gesh," a piercing in the area behind the scrotum, which he believed was the most erotic place to be pierced, despite its pain and discomfort. He eventually removed it after one of his children innocently questioned its presence during a shower. "He once had something called a geesh, GEISH, a geesh. This is a piercing of the area. It's the behind the scrotum."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's British Display Society Award
xref.body: After three years of art college, Dave Gahan earned a British Display Society Award, qualifying him to design store display windows. This provided a practical skill should his music career ever falter. "After three years, he ended up with something called a British Display Society Award. Which means if the singing thing ever falls through, he has qualified to design display windows for stores."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Embrace of Rock God Persona
xref.body: During the "Songs of Faith and Devotion" tour, Dave Gahan fully adopted a "rock god" image, which was visibly expressed through changes in his hairstyle and the acquisition of additional tattoos. One notable tattoo on his shoulder blades required a painful ten-hour session to complete. "Dave had totally embraced the rock god thing by this point. We saw changes in hairstyle, more tattoos, including one on his shoulder blades that took 10 painful hours."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's First Divorce and Remarriage
xref.body: Following a personal crisis, Dave Gahan left his first wife, Joanne, with whom he had a young son named Jack and had been married since the mid-1980s after knowing each other since their teenage years. He subsequently moved to Los Angeles, where he became romantically involved with Teresa Conway, Depeche Mode's former press officer, which resulted in the birth of a baby daughter. Gahan divorced Joanne and later married Teresa at the Graceland Chapel in Las Vegas, where an Elvis impersonator provided the wedding music. "Dave divorced Joanne and married Teresa at the Graceland Chapel in Las Vegas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Paranoia and Delusions
xref.body: Amidst his severe drug addiction, Dave Gahan developed extreme paranoia, leading him to carry a gun even for routine tasks like walking from his house to the mailbox. His mental state deteriorated into delusional behavior, including watching the Weather Channel for 24 consecutive hours, painting his walls and floor black, and engaging in conversations with his collection of stuffed animals, a behavior that became concerning when he claimed the animals began to speak back to him. "He grew paranoid and carried a gun, even just to get from the house to the mailbox."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Parental Issues
xref.body: Dave Gahan's childhood was affected by parental issues; his parents divorced when he was three, and his mother remarried. His stepfather was presented as his biological father until Dave discovered the truth at age 10, which profoundly impacted him. "Dave has had some issues regarding his parentage when he was three his parents divorced and his mom remarried. Stepdad was then present to Dave as his real dad. Stayed that way until he was 10, which is when he found out the truth, and that really messed him up for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Second Marriage and Tattoo
xref.body: Dave Gahan married his second wife, Teresa Conway, at the Graceland Chapel in Las Vegas, with an Elvis impersonator providing the music. As a pledge of love, Dave commissioned a tattoo reading "TC TTM/FG," which stands for "Teresa Conway to the motherf***ing Gahan." "Dave Gahan married his second wife Teresa Conway at the Graceland Chapel in Las Vegas. The music for the service was provided by an Alvison personator as part of Dave's pledge of love. He had a new tattoo commissioned yet rent TC TTM slash FG. It stands for Teresa Conway to the mother Blanker Gahan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Stalker Incident
xref.body: Dave Gahan faced extreme fan intrusion due to Depeche Mode's massive success, prompting him to move homes twice after repeatedly waking to fans singing on his lawn. In one alarming instance, a fan hired a private detective to track Gahan from the recording studio to his house to discover his address. "Dave had already moved twice because he kept waking up to find the Peshmoan fans singing on his front lawn."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Gahan's Teenage Delinquency and Art College
xref.body: As a teenager, Dave Gahan appeared in juvenile court three times for offenses like car theft and vandalism, and he held 20 different jobs within six months. His enrollment in art college was the only thing that saved him from a path of delinquency. "As a teenager, he went to juvenile court three times, for things like stealing cars and vandalism. He went through 20 different jobs in just six months."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dressing Room Arrangements on Tour
xref.body: On the road, Martin Gore and Andrew Fletcher share a dressing room, while Dave Gahan has his own. This arrangement is primarily attributed to Dave's need to avoid the temptations of backstage life. "When they're on the road, Martin and Andrew share a dressing room. Dave gets his own. That always more to Dave's need to be away from the temptations of backstage life than anything else."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Drug Dealer on Tour (Songs of Faith and Devotion Tour)
xref.body: Despite the presence of a psychiatrist, the 120-member staff on the "Songs of Faith and Devotion" tour also included a drug dealer. This individual was responsible for supplying members like Dave Gahan with cocaine and heroin, directly counteracting the psychiatrist's efforts to provide counseling for drug issues. "But then again, that 120 member staff also included a drug dealer to make sure that guys like Dave Gahan were well supplied with cocaine and heroin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Drug-Oriented Social Circle (Early 1990s)
xref.body: Dave Gahan was introduced to the social circle that hung around Jane's Addiction by Teresa Conroy, where drugs were consistently available, significantly contributing to his escalating substance abuse. "She introduced him to the people who hung around Jane's Diction, and there were always drugs available with that crowd."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early 90s Struggles
xref.body: In the early 1990s, Depeche Mode was in a "very bad place" largely due to extensive drug and alcohol use. Martin Gore suffered severe seizures, leading doctors to suspect a brain tumor. Andy Fletcher (Fletch) experienced debilitating panic attacks, and keyboardist Alan Wilder quit the band due to the stress. Singer Dave Gahan was heavily addicted to heroin and cocaine. "In the early 90s, Depeche Mode was in a very bad place. Thanks to lots and lots and lots of drugs and alcohol."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Heroin Addiction Development
xref.body: Dave Gahan initiated heroin use around 1991, rapidly progressing to a full-blown addiction by 1993. His residence in Los Angeles significantly exacerbated his drug problem, as drugs were easily accessible, especially after his second wife, Teresa, introduced him to the social circle associated with Jane's Addiction. "He had started using heroin in about 1991 and two years later he was a full-blown addict."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Incident with Hells Angels in Bardemodrid
xref.body: Three members of Depeche Mode were once beaten up by a group of Hells Angels outside of Bardemodrid. The incident was reportedly Dave Gahan's fault, as he looked at a biker girl "kind of funny." "Three members of the band were once beaten up by a group of hell's angels outside of Bardemodrid. Apparently it was Dave's fault for looking at a biker girl kind of funny."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mental Health Struggles (Early 1990s)
xref.body: Andy Fletcher was diagnosed with OCD, which he believed was inherited from his father, and also struggled with anxiety and depression, requiring professional treatment. He found Dave Gahan's ego trip particularly difficult to manage, contributing to a "three against Dave" dynamic within the band. "He was diagnosed with OCD, something he believed he inherited from his father."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musical Influences
xref.body: Bennington cited Scott Weiland of Stone Temple Pilots and Dave Gahan of Depeche Mode as his musical heroes, though the transcript notes these were "not exactly guys whose lifestyle should be emulated." "Although his heroes were Scott Wyland of the Stone Temple Pilots and Dave Gahn of Depeche Mode, not exactly guys whose lifestyle should be emulated."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Tour Health Crisis (Devotional Tour Aftermath)
xref.body: The aftermath of the Devotional Tour saw several band members facing severe health issues: Alan Wilder was diagnosed with kidney and gall stones during the South African leg; Andrew Fletcher nearly suffered a nervous breakdown and left the tour for treatment after his sister died of stomach cancer; Martin Gore experienced a grand mal seizure during a business meeting due to excessive drugs and alcohol; and Dave Gahan's severe drug use led to extreme weight loss (under 100 pounds) and an incident where he bit a journalist on the neck. "During the South African leg, Alan Wilder was diagnosed with kidney stones and then gall stones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Primal Scream's Reaction to Depeche Mode Tour Decadence
xref.body: Dave Gahan reportedly insisted that Primal Scream open for Depeche Mode on the Devotional Tour because he knew they enjoyed partying. However, Primal Scream was so appalled by the level of drug use and excess they witnessed that they allegedly gave up drugs entirely, despite their prior extensive use. "The story goes that primal scream was so shocked by what they saw that they gave up drugs entirely."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Psychiatrist on Tour (Songs of Faith and Devotion Tour)
xref.body: During the tour for "Songs of Faith and Devotion," the band hired a psychiatrist as part of their 120-member road crew, paying him $4,000 a week. This was intended to help band members, particularly Dave Gahan, with depression and addiction during the grueling 156 shows over 15 months, although the psychiatrist ended up being used by everyone but Dave. "This shrink was part of a 120 member staff that accompanied the band on the tour for the album Songs of Faith and Devotion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rehab Attempt (1990s)
xref.body: Shannon Hoon, the singer for Blind Melon, also attempted to get clean at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marino Del Rey, California, the same facility where Dave Gahan eventually found sobriety. "It was also where Shannon Hoon of Blind Melon tried to get straight."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Religious Background of Members
xref.body: Founding members Andrew Fletcher and Vince Clark were born-again Christians as teenagers, and their singing of hymns and devotional songs initially attracted Martin Gore and Dave Gahan, who were described as "essentially pagan unbelievers." Spiritually, Gore and Gahan have since "lapsed." "Andrew Fletcher and founding member Vince Clark were born again Christians as teenagers. Martin Gore and Dave Gahan, both essentially pagan unbelievers, were drawn to Andrew and Vince because they liked the hymns and devotional songs that they had heard Andrew and Vince sing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Sobriety and Continued Music Career (Late 1990s-Present)
xref.body: Martin Gore achieved sobriety midway through the recording of the "Ultra" album, which eased the rest of the recording process, particularly the vocal tracks. He continues to record and tour with Dave Gahan, maintaining a sober lifestyle. "Halfway through the recording of this record, Dave got clean and sober."

xref.title: Tour Overdose Incident (New Orleans)
xref.body: During a tour stop in New Orleans, Dave Gahan suffered an overdose of heroin between the end of the main set and the scheduled encore. This incident necessitated calling paramedics, and as a result, he was unable to return to the stage for the encore performance. "There was even an occasion in New Orleans where Dave couldn't do the encore because between the last song and the time he was supposed to go on stage for the encore, he owed deed and paramedics had to be called."

xref.title: Wedding Gift of Heroin
xref.body: Dave Gahan and his second wife, Teresa, were described as "rock and roll soulmates" who lived out a fantasy without considering the repercussions. A telling example of their lifestyle was receiving a large lump of black-tar heroin as one of their wedding presents. "And one of their favorite wedding presents just happened to be a big lump of black-tower heroin."
